options: A formal agreement between systems that defines the structure, format and rules of the data exchanged between them
A legal document for purchasing a database licence
An employment contract for data engineers
A service-level agreement for server uptime
A marketing agreement to share customer lists
questions.explanation: A data contract is a formal agreement between systems defining the structure, format and rules of exchanged data, including fields, types, constraints and validation rules.

questions.stem: Which architectural trends make clearly defined data contracts increasingly essential?
options: Microservices architectures, APIs and distributed systems
Monolithic applications with no external interfaces
questions.explanation: As businesses adopt microservices, APIs and distributed systems, clear data contracts become essential for seamless interoperability.

questions.stem: How do data contracts support interoperability?
options: By forcing all systems to use the same programming language
By storing all data in one central database
By allowing different systems, even those built with different technologies, to interact seamlessly through a common contract
By removing the need for validation
questions.explanation: By adhering to a common contract, different systems, even ones built with different technologies, can interact seamlessly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a component of a comprehensive data contract?
questions.explanation: The components are schema definition, validation rules, versioning strategy, error handling and responses, and security and compliance measures; pricing is not among them.

questions.stem: What does the validation rules component of a data contract define?
options: The programming language of the consumer
The encryption algorithm used in transit
How old versions are phased out
Constraints such as required fields, length limits and regex patterns
questions.explanation: Validation rules define constraints such as required fields, length limits and regex patterns that data must satisfy.

questions.stem: Which of the following technologies is listed as a compact and efficient format for serialising structured data when implementing data contracts?
questions.explanation: Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) is described as a compact and efficient format used for serialising structured data.

questions.stem: Which standard is used to define RESTful API structures, including request and response formats?
questions.explanation: The OpenAPI Specification defines RESTful API structures, including request and response formats.

questions.stem: Which schema-based serialisation framework is described as commonly used in big data applications?
questions.explanation: Avro is a schema-based serialisation framework commonly used in big data applications.

questions.stem: What is described as one of the biggest challenges in managing data contracts?
options: Choosing a colour for the documentation
Finding enough storage space for the contracts
Getting lawyers to sign each contract
Evolving them without breaking existing integrations
questions.explanation: One of the biggest challenges is evolving data contracts without breaking existing integrations, addressed by backward compatibility, deprecation strategies, feature flags and automated testing.

questions.stem: Which versioning best practice for data contracts introduces changes gradually so that consumers can adopt new features at their own pace?
questions.explanation: Feature flags introduce changes gradually and allow consumers to adopt new features at their own pace.
